scope: Five U13 changed-cue questions. Explicit hypothetical conditions replace careless-action giveaway wording. These are read-and-update tasks, not assessments of executed skating or guaranteed pass outcomes.

before.prompt: If D2 is closely marked before you release, what is sensible?

options.text: Reverse automatically because it was the original plan
Pass through D2’s marker without checking
Reassess a hold or another outlet

before.explanation: A closed second option means another read is needed; holding may be useful if possession can be protected.

after.prompt: You planned a reverse to D2. Before release, an opponent moves into that passing line. Which option has directly changed?

options.text: A pass toward W
A pass toward C
The reverse to D2

after.explanation: The reverse line to D2 is now occupied. Compare other outlets or protect the puck while you reassess. This hypothetical does not establish that W or C is open.

optionReasons.reason: W is another option to assess, but the stated change concerns D2.
C is another option to assess, but its availability is not established.
The opponent has entered the planned reverse line.

before.prompt: If Gold 1 follows your inward move, which response could help?

options.text: Call for a pass without looking at Gold 1
Reoffer elsewhere or make room for C
Remain still because your first move should have worked

before.explanation: A supporter should update the option; the first movement does not guarantee availability.

after.prompt: Gold 1 follows YOU inward and stays between YOU and D1. C has a separate clear line to D1. Which support option needs a new angle?

options.text: The pass from D1 to C
The pass from D1 to YOU
D1 keeping possession

after.explanation: The stated marker blocks the line to YOU. Reoffer at another angle while leaving C’s separate lane available. D1 still chooses whether to pass or retain the puck.

optionReasons.reason: The hypothetical explicitly leaves C’s line clear.
YOU need a different relationship to the marker to offer a clear line.
Retaining possession is a carrier decision, not the blocked support line.

before.prompt: Gold 1 moves directly onto your new lane. What might you do?

options.text: Rush beside F1 and remove the deeper option
Change the angle again or help clear F1’s route
Demand the same pass regardless

before.explanation: An option should be re-created when the marker moves.

after.prompt: Gold 1 enters the line from D1 to YOU. F1 still has a clear line to D1. Which move helps offer two separate passing options?

options.text: Move beside F1 on the same passing line
Find a different angle from F1, outside Gold 1’s line
Stay behind Gold 1 as a deeper target

after.explanation: Seek a separate angle so D1 can compare YOU and F1. Moving beside F1 may crowd one line; staying behind Gold 1 leaves the stated obstruction. The new angle must be checked as pressure changes.

optionReasons.reason: This gathers both supporters onto one line rather than offering separate routes.
This addresses the named blocker while preserving a separate F1 option.
Depth alone does not remove the blocker from the stated line.

before.prompt: Suppose Gold 1 follows your lateral move. What deserves another look?

options.text: The original shot as though Gold 1 had stayed still
A shot without checking the blocker
A pass to D2 or another change of angle

before.explanation: A moving defender can close the new lane, so alternatives remain relevant.

after.prompt: Gold 1 follows your lateral move and blocks the shot line. D2 has a clear passing line and room to receive. Which option uses that available support?

options.text: Shoot from the current position
Carry toward Gold 1
Pass to D2

after.explanation: A pass to D2 uses the support explicitly available in this hypothetical. Another carry or a later shot can become useful if the picture changes. The static scene alone does not guarantee reception or a successful next play.

optionReasons.reason: The hypothetical specifies an occupied shot line.
A carry can sometimes change pressure, but does not use the available D2 support.
This uses the clear support line named in the prompt.

before.prompt: If Gold 2 moves into your new route, what could you do?

options.text: Follow the route without looking
Change direction or stay as another support option
Insist on the return pass anyway

before.explanation: The pass does not obligate the receiver to return it; another support action may be better.

after.prompt: F2 still has the puck. Gold 2 blocks your planned return-pass route. Which adjustment offers F2 a different passing line?

options.text: Continue along that same route
Move to a new support angle
Call for the puck from the same spot

after.explanation: Offer a new angle and check it against Gold 2. F2 can keep possession or choose another play; a return pass is not owed. A call alone does not change the geometry, and a new angle is not automatically clear.

optionReasons.reason: Continuing on the specified route does not yet address its blocker.
A new angle changes the line for F2 to assess.
Communication helps coordination but does not by itself move the line.
